result:
The proposed answer is wrong. The solution never derives its formula; it ends on a guess after several candidate formulas failed.

A direct check at r = 2 shows the failure. Cay(Z_p, S) is triangle-free exactly when S is symmetric and sum-free, meaning no x, y in S have x + y in S. The largest sum-free subset of Z_p has size ⌊(p+1)/3⌋ when p ≡ 2 (mod 3) and ⌊(p−1)/3⌋... in any case at most about p/3, which is well below the guessed formula's value of roughly p/2.

For p = 13 the maximum sum-free set has size 4, so ex_Cay(K_3, Z_13) = 4 (the interval {5,…,8} is symmetric and sum-free). The proposed formula gives p − 1 − 2⌈(p−1)/(2r)⌉ = 12 − 2⌈12/4⌉ = 12 − 6 = 6, which exceeds 4. The formula therefore overshoots.

The formula does match the small cases p = 5, 7, 11 at r = 2, which is why it can look plausible. It also matches the endpoints r = 1 and r = p − 1, but the p = 13 case is a counterexample.

VERDICT: REJECT
